items.question_text: A GP sees a well 40-year-old for a 6-minute chat about a holiday. The receptionist asks which Medicare item to bill. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Bill a level B. Any attendance can be claimed
Do not bill a consultation. No clinically relevant service was provided
Bill a health assessment. He is an adult
Bill the consultation to his wife's card because she is a regular patient
Bill a care plan. It can be backdated
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

B. Do not bill a consultation. No clinically relevant service was provided

---

1. CLINICAL SITUATION
A GP sees a well 40-year-old for a 6-minute chat about a holiday. The receptionist asks which Medicare item to bill.

2. THE RULE
Medicare benefits are claimed only for a clinically relevant service personally provided, never double-billed to a public hospital service.

3. WHY B IS CORRECT
A Medicare benefit is for a clinically relevant service. A social chat with no clinical content is not one. Using another person's card is a separate offence.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. Bill a level B. Any attendance can be claimed: Attendance alone is not enough.
C. Bill a health assessment. He is an adult: No assessment was done.
D. Bill the consultation to his wife's card because she is a regular patient: Another person's Medicare card is not available for use.
E. Bill a care plan. It can be backdated: There is no plan, and backdating is false.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
Medicare benefits are claimed only for a clinically relevant service personally provided, never double-billed to a public hospital service.

---

items.question_text: A practice bulk-bills a level C and also asks the patient for a $40 facility fee in cash, not receipted. The patient is a pensioner. What is the most appropriate view?
options: Acceptable if the patient is not told it is compulsory
Not acceptable. Bulk-billing means the benefit is full payment
Acceptable if the fee is under $50
Acceptable. A facility fee is outside Medicare
Acceptable for pensioners only
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

B. Not acceptable. Bulk-billing means the benefit is full payment

---

1. CLINICAL SITUATION
Do not take the $40. Bulk-billing is full payment.

2. THE RULE
Bulk-billing means accepting the Medicare benefit as full payment, so no additional charge can be added.

3. WHY B IS CORRECT
If a service is bulk-billed, the practitioner accepts the Medicare benefit as full payment for that service. An extra undisclosed cash fee is not permitted.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. Acceptable if the patient is not told it is compulsory: Not telling her does not make it lawful.
C. Acceptable if the fee is under $50: There is no such allowance.
D. Acceptable. A facility fee is outside Medicare: Calling it a facility fee does not take it outside the agreement.
E. Acceptable for pensioners only: The rule is not limited by concession status.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
Bulk-billing accepts the benefit as full payment.

---

items.question_text: A man asks you to prescribe his own statin onto his wife's PBS script because she has reached the safety net and he has not. Using a spouse's concession or safety net is a false claim. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Agree for statins only
Agree. Safety-net sharing within a couple is allowed
Write it in her name and document 'household use'
Agree if he pays the difference
Decline. A PBS prescription is for the person who needs the medicine
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

E. Decline. A PBS prescription is for the person who needs the medicine

---

1. CLINICAL SITUATION
Decline. His statin does not go on her script.

2. THE RULE
A PBS prescription is written only for the person who clinically needs the medicine and is named on it.

3. WHY E IS CORRECT
A PBS prescription is written for the patient who clinically needs that medicine. Using a spouse's concession or safety net is a false claim.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. Agree for statins only: The drug class is irrelevant.
B. Agree. Safety-net sharing within a couple is allowed: It is not.
C. Write it in her name and document 'household use': Documentation of a falsehood is worse.
D. Agree if he pays the difference: Paying a gap does not fix a script in the wrong name.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
A PBS script is for the named patient.

---

items.question_text: A GP sees an Aboriginal man who is not registered for Closing the Gap. He writes CTG on the script and tells him the pharmacy will charge the lower co-payment. The annotation works only after that. What is the most appropriate correction?
options: CTG applies automatically to every Aboriginal patient
Ask the pharmacist to register him at the counter
Register him properly first. An annotation alone does not create eligibility
Use a relative's CTG registration
The annotation is enough. Registration is optional
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

C. Register him properly first. An annotation alone does not create eligibility

---

1. CLINICAL SITUATION
Register him. Writing CTG on the script is not enough.

2. THE RULE
Closing the Gap PBS co-payment relief needs a one-off registration by a PBS prescriber or Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Practitioner; writing CTG on a script (optional since July 2021) or asking a pharmacist does not create eligibility.

3. WHY C IS CORRECT
Closing the Gap PBS registration is a one-off clinical registration. The annotation works only after that. A pharmacist cannot create it, and it is not automatic.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. CTG applies automatically to every Aboriginal patient: It does not.
B. Ask the pharmacist to register him at the counter: Registration is clinical, not a counter act.
D. Use a relative's CTG registration: Registration is individual.
E. The annotation is enough. Registration is optional: Registration is the step that creates eligibility.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
CTG needs registration before annotation.

---

items.question_text: A 34-week pregnant woman in a small rural hospital has a blood pressure of 170/110 and headache, not settling with first-line treatment. The on-call GP plans to observe overnight because the flying doctor is busy and the road is two hours. A small hospital cannot provide the level she needs. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Discharge to the local motel near the hospital
Transfer by private car with no escort
Observe overnight. Retrieval is for daytime only
Treat as pre-eclampsia and arrange urgent retrieval. Do not wait out the night
Start treatment and review in the antenatal clinic next week
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

D. Treat as pre-eclampsia and arrange urgent retrieval. Do not wait out the night

---

1. CLINICAL SITUATION
Treat and retrieve tonight. Do not observe severe pre-eclampsia in a small hospital.

2. THE RULE
Rural clinicians arrange timely retrieval or transfer when a patient needs a higher level of care and defer elective procedures when safe resources are unavailable.

3. WHY D IS CORRECT
This is severe pre-eclampsia. A small hospital cannot provide the obstetric and neonatal level she needs. Busy is not a reason to hold an unstable patient. Private car is not a retrieval.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. Discharge to the local motel near the hospital: Proximity to the building is not care.
B. Transfer by private car with no escort: An unescorted car is not a retrieval.
C. Observe overnight. Retrieval is for daytime only: Urgency is clinical, not clerical.
E. Start treatment and review in the antenatal clinic next week: Next week is not a safe interval.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
Retrieval follows clinical need, not the clock.

---

Acceptable. Any registered clinician may open any record
Acceptable if the record is already populated
Acceptable if he does not tell anyone

Do not open it. He is not your patient.

Access to a My Health Record needs a legitimate purpose in the person's care. Curiosity about a celebrity is not one. Secrecy does not repair it.

C. Acceptable. Any registered clinician may open any record: Registration is not a browsing right.
D. Acceptable if the record is already populated: Content does not create a purpose.
E. Acceptable if he does not tell anyone: An undisclosed breach is still a breach.

My Health Record access needs a care purpose.

items.question_text: A patient is seen in a public emergency department for a sprained ankle, at no charge. The visiting GP also bills a Medicare consultation for the same attendance. What is the most appropriate view?
options: Acceptable if the patient agrees
Acceptable if the sprain is mild
Acceptable. Hospital and Medicare are different payers
Acceptable for after-hours only
Not acceptable. The same public-hospital service is not also bulk-billed to Medicare
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

E. Not acceptable. The same public-hospital service is not also bulk-billed to Medicare

---

1. CLINICAL SITUATION
Do not bill Medicare for the same public ED attendance.

2. THE RULE
Medicare benefits are claimed only for a clinically relevant service personally provided, never double-billed to a public hospital service.

3. WHY E IS CORRECT
A service provided as part of a public hospital attendance is not also claimed on Medicare by the same doctor for the same occasion. Patient agreement does not create a second benefit.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. Acceptable if the patient agrees: The patient cannot authorise a duplicate claim.
B. Acceptable if the sprain is mild: Severity is irrelevant.
C. Acceptable. Hospital and Medicare are different payers: Different payers do not mean two fees for one service.
D. Acceptable for after-hours only: The hour does not change it.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
One public-hospital service is not claimed twice.

items.question_text: An online service offers a new patient, never examined, a benzodiazepine script after a 90-second chat, and bills a long telehealth consult. A telehealth consult must still be a proper clinical service, and the item billed must match what was done. What is the most appropriate view?
options: Acceptable if the script is for five tablets
Acceptable because the patient requested it
Acceptable. Telehealth has no rules about length or drugs
Acceptable if the patient is rural
Not acceptable. No adequate assessment, and a long-consult item is not earned
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

E. Not acceptable. No adequate assessment, and a long-consult item is not earned

---

Decline the model. A 90-second script is not a long consult.

Telehealth services require an adequate clinical assessment and are billed with the MBS item that matches the service actually provided.

A telehealth consult must still be a proper clinical service, and the item billed must match what was done. A 90-second chat with a stranger for a drug of dependence is neither.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. Acceptable if the script is for five tablets: Quantity does not repair the assessment.
B. Acceptable because the patient requested it: A request is not a clinical indication.
C. Acceptable. Telehealth has no rules about length or drugs: It has both.
D. Acceptable if the patient is rural: Rural location does not lower the standard.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
Telehealth is still clinical care.

---

A GP management plan is for a patient with a chronic condition, prepared with them. Age is not an indication. An unseen template is not a plan.

A care plan needs a chronic condition and the patient.

items.question_text: A GP wants to bill a 715 health assessment for an Aboriginal man who is an inpatient for pneumonia, having had a 715 four months ago. A 715 is a practice-based assessment, not a hospital inpatient item, and it is not claimed more often than the set interval. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Bill it. Inpatient status does not matter
Bill a 715 every admission
Bill it to complete the hospital discharge
Do not bill. He is an inpatient, and the interval has not elapsed
Bill it if the pneumonia is resolving
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

D. Do not bill. He is an inpatient, and the interval has not elapsed

---

Do not bill a 715. He is in hospital and had one four months ago.

2. THE RULE
The MBS 715 health assessment is offered on self-identification as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander, at least 9 months apart, to a non-admitted patient, never to a hospital inpatient.

3. WHY D IS CORRECT
A 715 is a practice-based assessment, not a hospital inpatient item, and it is not claimed more often than the set interval.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. Bill it. Inpatient status does not matter: It does.
B. Bill a 715 every admission: That is not the program.
C. Bill it to complete the hospital discharge: Discharge is not a 715.
E. Bill it if the pneumonia is resolving: Recovery does not create eligibility.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
A 715 is not for an inpatient.

---

items.question_text: A rural GP obstetrician is asked to start an elective caesarean at 39 weeks. The hospital has no after-hours theatre nurse tonight, no blood on site, and the nearest backup is three hours away. Mother and baby are well. An elective case waits for a safe service. What is the most appropriate plan?
options: Start and ask a midwife to scrub
Discharge her to labour at home
Defer. Do not start elective surgery without staff, blood, and a realistic backup
Start. Elective caesarean is always safer in labour ward
Start under local anaesthetic to avoid the gap
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

C. Defer. Do not start elective surgery without staff, blood, and a realistic backup

---

1. CLINICAL SITUATION
Do not start. An elective caesarean waits for a safe theatre.

2. THE RULE
Rural clinicians arrange timely retrieval or transfer when a patient needs a higher level of care and defer elective procedures when safe resources are unavailable.

3. WHY C IS CORRECT
An elective case waits for a safe service. Starting without theatre staff or blood, hours from help, creates a risk she does not need tonight.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. Start and ask a midwife to scrub: Improvising the team is not a service.
B. Discharge her to labour at home: Deferring the operation is not abandoning antenatal care.
D. Start. Elective caesarean is always safer in labour ward: Safer than what is not established, and the conditions are absent.
E. Start under local anaesthetic to avoid the gap: Anaesthetic choice does not replace blood and help.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
Do not start elective rural surgery without backup.

---

items.question_text: A patient needs a restricted PBS antibiotic. The GP writes the script with authority pending and tells the pharmacist to dispense a full PBS quantity. Pending is not approved. What is the most appropriate correction?
options: Use another patient's authority number
Do not claim a PBS quantity until the authority is actually held
Ask the patient to sign that they accept the restriction
Annotate CTG instead of an authority
Dispense. Pending is the same as approved
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

B. Do not claim a PBS quantity until the authority is actually held

---

1. CLINICAL SITUATION
Get the authority first. Pending is not approval.

2. THE RULE
A PBS authority must be obtained when the restriction requires it before the PBS quantity is prescribed or claimed.

3. WHY B IS CORRECT
An authority restriction means the authority comes first. Pending is not approved. Another patient's number, or a CTG annotation, does not replace it.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. Use another patient's authority number: That is a false claim.
C. Ask the patient to sign that they accept the restriction: The patient cannot authorise a restricted benefit.
D. Annotate CTG instead of an authority: CTG is a co-payment scheme, not an authority.
E. Dispense. Pending is the same as approved: It is not.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
An authority restriction is met before the PBS claim.

---

Not acceptable. A routine repeat is not an urgent after-hours service
Acceptable if he has no tablets left
Acceptable. Any 10 pm contact is urgent
Acceptable if the clinic is open

B. Not acceptable. A routine repeat is not an urgent after-hours service

---

An extra fee added to a bulk-billed consultation.

2. THE RULE
Bulk-billing means accepting the Medicare benefit as full payment, so no additional charge can be added.

When a doctor bulk bills, the patient assigns the Medicare benefit and the doctor accepts it as full payment for the service. Under the Health Insurance Act 1973 (Cth), charging the patient an additional amount for that service, including booking or administration fees, is not allowed.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. It is acceptable because admin fees are not Medicare services: Charges connected to a bulk-billed service are prohibited.
B. It is acceptable for children only: There is no exception for children.
D. It is acceptable if the fee is displayed in reception: Displaying the fee does not make it lawful.
E. It is acceptable if the parent agrees in writing: Written agreement does not override the rules.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
Bulk billing means no additional charge for that service.

items.question_text: A 58-year-old man presents to a small rural hospital with an anterior STEMI that began 1 hour ago. The nearest PCI-capable hospital is 3 hours away by road or air. There are no contraindications to thrombolysis. What is the most appropriate management?
options: Give aspirin only and transfer next day
Transfer for primary PCI without fibrinolysis
Observe locally and repeat the ECG in 6 hours
Give fibrinolysis promptly, ideally within 30 minutes of arrival, and arrange transfer to the PCI centre
Wait for troponin before deciding
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

D. Give fibrinolysis promptly, ideally within 30 minutes of arrival, and arrange transfer to the PCI centre

---

1. CLINICAL SITUATION
STEMI in a rural hospital far from PCI.

2. THE RULE
Rural clinicians arrange timely retrieval or transfer when a patient needs a higher level of care and defer elective procedures when safe resources are unavailable.

3. WHY D IS CORRECT
When primary PCI cannot be delivered within about 120 minutes of first medical contact, the Australian ACS guideline recommends fibrinolysis without delay (door-to-needle within 30 minutes) for eligible patients, followed by transfer to a PCI-capable centre for further management.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. Give aspirin only and transfer next day: Aspirin alone is inadequate for STEMI.
B. Transfer for primary PCI without fibrinolysis: A 3-hour delay to PCI loses myocardium; fibrinolysis is preferred.
C. Observe locally and repeat the ECG in 6 hours: Delay increases mortality.
E. Wait for troponin before deciding: STEMI is diagnosed on ECG; troponin is not awaited.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
If PCI is more than 120 min away, give fibrinolysis then transfer.

---

items.question_text: An unconscious 50-year-old woman arrives in ED after a collapse. Her My Health Record has access controls set, so some documents are restricted. The team needs her medication list to manage her safely, and no relative can be reached. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Wait until she wakes to ask permission
Do not access the record because she set restrictions
Use emergency access to view her My Health Record, which is permitted to lessen a serious threat when consent cannot be obtained, and document the reason
Access the record of her husband instead
Ask the hospital IT department to remove her restrictions
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

C. Use emergency access to view her My Health Record, which is permitted to lessen a serious threat when consent cannot be obtained, and document the reason

---

1. CLINICAL SITUATION
An unconscious patient with a restricted My Health Record.

2. THE RULE
Clinicians access a patient's My Health Record only for a legitimate clinical purpose within a care relationship.

3. WHY C IS CORRECT
The My Health Records Act 2012 (Cth) allows emergency access when it is unreasonable or impracticable to obtain consent and access is needed to lessen or prevent a serious threat to the person's life, health or safety. Each emergency access is logged and must be justified.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. Wait until she wakes to ask permission: Waiting may cause harm.
B. Do not access the record because she set restrictions: Emergency access is specifically permitted in this situation.
D. Access the record of her husband instead: Accessing a relative's record is unauthorised.
E. Ask the hospital IT department to remove her restrictions: Clinicians cannot remove a person's access controls.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
Emergency access to My Health Record is lawful to prevent a serious threat.

Bill the telehealth item and record a face-to-face visit later

Bill the telehealth item because video consults are always rebated

A new patient requests a rebated video consultation.

Telehealth services require an adequate clinical assessment and are billed with the MBS item that matches the service actually provided.

Most GP telehealth items need an established clinical relationship.

items.question_text: At 10 pm the on-call GP gives telephone advice to a man with mild hay fever symptoms and tells him to see his usual GP during the week. The practice asks to bill an urgent after-hours face-to-face attendance item. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Bill the urgent face-to-face item
Bill a 715 health assessment
Do not bill a face-to-face urgent attendance item; no face-to-face service was provided and the problem was not urgent
Bill a GP chronic condition management plan
Bill a home visit item
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

C. Do not bill a face-to-face urgent attendance item; no face-to-face service was provided and the problem was not urgent

---

1. CLINICAL SITUATION
Phone advice for a non-urgent problem after hours.

2. THE RULE
Urgent after-hours items are billed only for genuinely urgent services in after-hours periods, not routine repeat prescriptions.

3. WHY C IS CORRECT
An MBS item must match the service actually provided. A face-to-face attendance item cannot be billed for phone advice, and urgent after-hours items require a condition needing urgent assessment. Mild hay fever is not urgent.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. Bill the urgent face-to-face item: Billing a face-to-face item for phone advice is a false claim.
B. Bill a 715 health assessment: A 715 is a specific health assessment.
D. Bill a GP chronic condition management plan: No chronic condition plan was prepared.
E. Bill a home visit item: No home visit took place.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
Bill only the service provided; phone advice is not a face-to-face urgent attendance.
